name: The M: Micro Transit

name: METRO Connect

name: ORT On-Demand
area: Northwest Arkansas city zones: Fayetteville, Springdale, Rogers (Mon-Sat); Bentonville (Sat only)

Program began in Rogers ~2020 and expanded to Bentonville/Fayetteville Feb 2022 (2 buses each in Rogers/Bentonville at that time); ride requests grew from ~500/week (Feb 2022) to ~1,500/week (Jul 2022).

name: DART Connect
area: Three on-demand zones: Georgetown and Millsboro (Sussex County) and Newark (New Castle County), DE
operator: Delaware Transit Corporation (DART First State), a division of DelDOT
booking: App (DART Transit / DART Connect app), Phone (1-800-652-DART, Option 3)

fleet: Minibuses / mini-transit buses (~11 seats each; Newark launched with two vehicles)

Newark added Aug 2023, replacing the Unicity fixed-route loop. Waits estimated no more than 15 min. Available to the general public; first/last-mile connections to regular DART routes.

name: Hele-On Ka Hoʻokele (Rural Door-to-Door Service)

Registration required; reservations at (808) 731-7009 option 3, minimum one day in advance, up to 14 days ahead. Riders travel within a district or are taken to the nearest Hele-On fixed-route stop for onward travel.

name: DART On Demand
area: Des Moines metro — Ankeny microtransit zone (active); Clive, Urbandale and Altoona zones planned fall 2026 under Reimagine DART
operator: Des Moines Area Regional Transit Authority (DART)

notes: Point-to-point on-demand shared rides within a defined zone using smaller buses; trips can be booked in real-time or scheduled in advance and may be shared. Ankeny zone runs as-is until Sept 28, 2026, then reconfigured Ankeny plus new Clive-Urbandale and Altoona zones launch fall 2026 under Reimagine DART. Ankeny zone bounds: NE 62nd Ave (south), SE Four Mile Dr (east), 36th St (north), SW Irvinedale Dr (west).

name: EASE (East Ames Service Extension)
area: East Ames on-demand zone, Ames, IA (pickups within EASE zone plus Ames City Hall)
operator: CyRide (City of Ames / Iowa State University transit)
fare: $1.00 per trip (same as regular CyRide bus fare)
notes: Curb-to-curb on-demand service; riders use the Ride Pingo app or call CyRide (515-239-5600, at least 30 min ahead for call-ins). Pingo platform launched with CyRide Dec 2022 — The Routing Company's first Midwest on-demand agency partnership. Two-year TRC contract awarded Oct 2022; agency reported improved efficiency, reduced call-center volume, high rider satisfaction. Transfers to fixed routes at City Hall.

name: HIRTA On-Demand
area: Boone, Dallas, Jasper, Madison, Marion, Story and Warren counties (central Iowa)

name: Peoplerides

fare: In-town $2-$15 depending on county/city; out-of-town demand-response $2.89 per mile
notes: Established 1974; open to the general public including persons with disabilities; provides 50,000+ rides annually across the four counties using 20 ADA-accessible vehicles; offers both route and demand-response trips. Advance booking (at least one day) receives priority; same-day depends on driver availability. Medicaid-funded trips booked via broker (MTM); Marshalltown paratransit requires prior approval.

name: Region 8 Regional Transit Authority (RTA) On-Demand
area: Delaware, Dubuque (excl. City of Dubuque) and Jackson counties, northeast Iowa (Planning Area 8)
fleet: ~30 light-duty buses and accessible minivans; transitioning to 9-passenger vans
notes: Modernized rural demand-response using QRyde booking/routing/scheduling platform; ~100,000 passenger trips annually serving ~2,500 individuals. Advance reservations typically requested 24h ahead; same-day available subject to availability; ~10-min-out arrival notifications. Open to the general public; all vehicles wheelchair accessible.

name: River Bend Transit
area: Cedar, Clinton, Muscatine and Scott counties (Iowa Quad Cities region)

FTA transit agency profile ID 70049.

name: SEIBUS (Southeast Iowa Bus)

Iowa DOT classifies it as Demand-Response, Subscription. Ridership figures not found.

name: SWITA (Southwest Iowa Transit Agency)

area: Within Bloomington city limits (Downtown, East, and North zones); serves trips not within walkable distance of a fixed bus route

notes: No eligibility or application required; rides booked on demand or up to 24 hours in advance. Repeated no-shows/late cancellations may result in booking restrictions.

name: Hamilton County Express
area: Hamilton County, IN (Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Westfield and contiguous counties)

name: METS Micro
area: City of Evansville, Indiana (designated on-demand zones; expanding to Jacobsville)

notes: Curb-to-curb on-demand shared-ride service open to the general public, book any two points in town; booked via Lawrence Transit On Demand app (Spare, iOS/Android) or phone (785) 312-7054. Ridership/performance data not published on site.

name: Night Line
area: Within Lawrence city limits, Douglas County, KS

CATS also runs a separate 'CATS on Demand' service (~10,000 rides/month) whose relationship to LYNX is unclear from available sources.

Fare/hours/fleet/vendor/funding not confirmed this pass.

Requires 3 business days' advance notice to schedule a ride. Open to the general public, with additional coordinated services for elderly, MaineCare recipients, veterans, and people with disabilities. Contact: 207-973-3695 or 1-866-853-5969.

name: Metro Connect (Falmouth)
operator: Greater Portland Metro (GPMetro / Greater Portland Transit District)

notes: GPMetro's first microtransit program; door-to-zone on-demand shuttle open to the general public, booked through the Spare Rider platform (vendor confirmed via booking URL). Per a Nov 2025 one-year-in review, averaging ~1 ride/hour with a goal of 2 rides/hour by end of 2025. Service area has expanded to cover most of Falmouth since a December 2024 launch.

name: Mid-Coast Connector (WCAP Transportation Services)
area: Waldo, Knox, Lincoln, and Sagadahoc Counties, plus Brunswick and Harpswell, ME (fixed-route DASH service separately in Belfast/Rockland)
fare: Not specified (varies by service type/distance; reduced fares for seniors, children under 17, and disabled riders reported for DASH and senior medical trips)
notes: WCAP operates flex-route/demand-response service open to the general public plus MaineCare non-emergency medical transportation, distinct from its fixed-route DASH city bus service in Belfast/Rockland. Confirmed via Maine Transit Association member listing and WCAP's own program page.

name: RTP (Regional Transportation Program)
area: Cumberland County, Maine (includes Lakes Region Explorer route between Bridgton and Portland)
notes: Shared-ride demand-response service prioritizing elderly, disabled, and low-income riders but explicitly open to the general public; requires advance phone booking (same-day changes must be called in, not made online). Separately offers ADA-compliant paratransit (ADA Rider Application/Policy) not separately catalogued here.

name: RTP Catch-A-Ride
fare: $2.50 (same town/neighboring towns), $5.00 (non-adjoining towns); many riders qualify for free service via application
notes: General-public, county-wide shared-ride demand-response service; RTP states it serves 'anyone' in Cumberland County on a space-available basis. NOT disability-restricted -- that description (people 'prevented by a disability from utilizing fixed-route bus service') applies to RTP's separate ADA paratransit program, not Catch-A-Ride. Booking is phone-only (774-2666 or 800-244-0704); no app booking found on the source page despite candidate's 'Phone, App' claim. Requires up to 2 weeks advance booking, minimum 2 business days notice -- not same-day.

name: Standish-Gorham Microtransit Pilot
area: Standish and Gorham (RTP also serves Raymond, Windham, and a separate Harrison pilot), Cumberland County, ME
notes: Launched October 15, 2025; same-day on-demand home pickup to any destination within service area. Funded through at least May 2026, with a $6 fare extension to downtown Portland reportedly proposed. Distinct from RTP's separate Harrison pilot ($99,576 grant) and from RTP's general advance-reservation (2+ business days) demand-response/paratransit service.

name: Western Maine Transportation Services (WMTS)
area: Androscoggin, Oxford, and Franklin Counties, plus Bath and Brunswick, ME
notes: Demand-response service open to the general public across three western Maine counties plus Bath/Brunswick; site also lists separate flex, fixed, and commuter routes (not in scope). Fares reported unchanged since Oct 1, 2019 (amount not specified).

name: GEST (Liberty/Gladstone, MO)

notes: General-public, door-to-door, on-demand service; replaced a discontinued IRIS microtransit service (IRIS ended late Sept 2025 due to rising costs). Liberty launched ~1 week before article, Gladstone ~1 month prior; Liberty saw a 140% week-over-week ridership increase and up to 50 rides/day expected; Gladstone completed 'hundreds of rides.' Liberty is running a 30-day pilot before deciding on contract extension. Vehicles are NOT ADA-compliant — riders needing accommodation are directed to Liberty Access Bus or separate GEST paratransit option. Some riders reported being unable to book rides despite operator claims of full availability.

name: IRIS (Independence)

fare: $5.00 per person per trip (free to/from 4 designated transfer points: Independence Transit Center, Centerpoint Medical Center, Independence Municipal Commons, Blue Ridge transfer point)
notes: Dynamic-routing microtransit covering entire Independence city limits, pickup/dropoff within ~1/4 mile of requested locations. Candidate's original fare ($3.00) and fleet ('Not specified') were incorrect/incomplete per official city source; corrected here. One secondary April 2025 news report suggested planned cessation May 1 2025, but the live official city page (checked July 2026) states the service is currently active — worth flagging in concerns.csv if added. Launch year conflicting (candidate: 2023; one news summary: Jan 2025) and unconfirmed from a primary source, left as Not specified.

name: Dawson County Transit
notes: Weekday dial-a-ride service; serves Dawson County High School, downtown Glendive, Glendive Dinosaur and Fossil Museum, Glendive Medical Center, and the Glendive bus stop. Phone reservation line (406) 377-5024.

Official qac.org pages for the service returned 404 on every URL tried (qac.org/198/Transportation, qac.org/162/County-Ride); no working official website located. Operator name corrected from candidate's 'Queen Anne's County Government' to the more specific verified 'Queen Anne's County Department of Aging' per LOTS.

name: Ride On Flex
area: Montgomery County, MD (Zone 918 — Sandy Spring/White Oak, New Hampshire Ave corridor)
operator: Montgomery County Department of Transportation (Ride On)
booking: App (Ride On Flex app, iOS/Android) or phone call to 240-301-3842; call center hours Mon-Fri 6am-7pm
notes: As of July 1, 2026 the Rockville and Glenmont/Wheaton zones were discontinued; only Zone 918 (Sandy Spring/White Oak, along New Hampshire Ave from Cloverly St to Lockwood Dr/White Oak Center) continues operating. Same-day on-demand booking only, no fixed schedule. Not to be confused with fixed-route Ride On bus service. Won a 2020 NACo Innovation Award.

name: Shore Ride (Shore Transit)
area: Wicomico, Worcester, and Somerset Counties, MD (Lower Eastern Shore)
operator: Shore Transit (Tri-County Council for the Lower Eastern Shore of Maryland)
booking: Phone reservation via Shore Transit Customer Service Center (443-260-2300)
fare: $5.00 per ride (general public); $4.00 per ride for elderly/disabled riders in Wicomico County
hours: Not specified (operates during fixed-route service hours, which vary by county)
notes: General-public rural demand-response service for riders who live 3/4 mile or more beyond a fixed-route stop or transfer point, across the 3-county Lower Eastern Shore service area (Somerset, Wicomico, Worcester). Requires reservation by noon the day prior to travel. Distinct from Shore Transit's separately branded 'Shore Access' ADA origin-to-destination paratransit service (also $5/ride, restricted to riders whose disability prevents fixed-route use).

name: DJ Transit (Southern Connect)
fleet: Buses, vans, and wheelchair-accessible (ADA-compliant) vehicles; fleet size and capacity not specified
notes: Community transportation provider based in Laurel, MS (1010 Rogers Street). Site confirms rides must be scheduled at least 24 hours ahead by phone, open to general public for work, school, shopping, business, and medical trips. Branded 'Southern Connect' on MDOT's ConnectMS regional network page, which independently confirms the same phone number and describes the region as serving 13 counties in south Mississippi. Buses serve employment/school/senior routes within Jones County; vans and wheelchair-accessible vehicles serve broader medical/shopping/recreational trips. Fare details exist only in a downloadable PDF/PPT not retrievable via fetch.

name: Delta Rides
area: Northwest Mississippi Delta (21 counties per MDOT ConnectMS)
operator: Regional network of nonprofit transportation providers in the Mississippi Delta, coordinated via a shared call center under MDOT's ConnectMS program (37 partner agencies including transit agencies, nonprofits, and Mississippi Valley State University)
notes: Regional mobility-coordination network covering 21+ counties in NW Mississippi Delta; MDOT ConnectMS page describes it as 'a call center that provides connectivity between the systems' offering rides to employment, medical centers and other destinations. Own site states general 'families and communities' framing with no stated eligibility restriction (not ADA/senior-limited); phone-only reservation, no app/online booking found. Distinct from the state's only other inventoried MS system (Coast Transit Authority ADA Paratransit), which is a different region, operator, and eligibility model entirely.

name: SMART
notes: Listed by MDOT's ConnectMS as the regional mobility-coordination network for 13 counties in southwest Mississippi, providing non-emergency medical transportation, employment trips, and college shuttles. Corroborated independently by the Mississippi Public Transit Association resources page, which names the operator as S.M.A.R.T Regional Group. No independent operator website located across two research passes; eligibility criteria for general-public access not explicitly documented on either source.

name: TRANS-CON (Transportation Connection)
area: Central Mississippi (Copiah, Hinds, Madison, Rankin, Simpson, Warren, Yazoo counties)
notes: Regional mobility-coordination network for 7 counties in central Mississippi, listed on MDOT's ConnectMS program page. Independent search confirmed the operator as Jackson Medical Mall Foundation and the full county list. MDOT describes the service as offering vanpool/commuter employment trips, non-emergency medical transportation, and student transportation to local colleges/universities — these read as example trip purposes under a general-public rural transit umbrella (per ConnectMS's own general description of its network), not confirmed eligibility restrictions, but this distinction was not independently verified beyond the MDOT page. No independent TRANS-CON or Jackson Medical Mall Foundation page with fare/hours/fleet/vendor details was located.

name: RideMon
area: Morgantown / Monongalia County (microtransit zone covering Mountain Heights and Grafton Road areas, connecting to Mountaineer Mall, Hornbeck Road Walmart, and Sabraton Goodwill)
fare: $0.75 per passenger (same as fixed-route bus fare)
notes: Launched May 9, 2022 as a six-month pilot replacing coverage on low-performing Route 14 (Mt. Heights) and Route 15 (Grafton Road); originally booked via Uber's app under an Uber partnership, which ended June 2023 when the program switched to Spare's on-demand platform (current vendor). As of July 2026 the service had surpassed 15,000 total rides with roughly 600 rides/month, and RideMon ridership reportedly began outnumbering bus ridership in the same zone within about four months of launch.

name: Ready Ride (PVTA)
area: Grant, Hardy, Hampshire, and Mineral Counties, WV (town-based zones in Petersburg, Moorefield, Romney, and Keyser)
vendor: Spare (inferred from Google Play package name for the 'Ride PVTA' app; not independently confirmed on PVTA's own site)
fare: $2.00 per boarding (current site); one earlier PVTA social post cited $1.50 per boarding — discrepancy unresolved, may reflect a fare change over time
hours: Monday-Friday (specific hours vary by zone; not fully published)
notes: On-demand, no-fixed-route service that picks up multiple passengers within defined town zones; explicitly distinguished by PVTA from both fixed-route and NEMT/Medicaid transport. Petersburg zone launched July 1, 2019; Romney and Moorefield followed the same year; Keyser zone added around October 2019 (exact date unconfirmed). PVTA's separate Non-Emergency Medical Transport service (Medicaid-eligibility-restricted) is out of scope and not this row. PVTA also operates a distinct 'route deviation' fixed-route service, also out of scope.

name: Here and There Transit (Demand Response)
area: Barbour County and portions of Taylor County, WV
operator: Barbour County Senior Center, Inc. dba Here and There Transit Authority
fare: Distance-based: $2.25 (up to 10 mi) to $3.00 (30+ mi within county); $1.00/extra stop; $8.00 out-of-county shopping trips; $16.00 Morgantown trips
funding: FTA Section 5311 (rural formula, per WVDOT subrecipient status) plus local match; not itemized further
fleet: 15 revenue vehicles per 2022 NTD data (mix of demand-response and fixed-route fleet, not broken out); wheelchair-lift-equipped
notes: Door-to-door reservation-based service open to the general public throughout Barbour County (reserve travel from home to any in-county destination); distinct from the same operator's fixed 'Blue & Gray Loop' shuttle in Philippi (9 daily weekday trips, out of scope as fixed-schedule) and from its Non-Emergency Medical Transport program (Medicaid/sliding-scale, described separately from general demand-response on the rider's guide). Prior-day reservation required ('at least the day before'); same-day not offered per site language, consistent with Advance scheduling window.

name: Aberdeen Ride Line
area: Aberdeen and within 2.5 miles of city limits
notes: Open to the general public, all ages, no membership required, any trip purpose, per the city's own Ride Line page. Rides must be scheduled by 4:00 PM the prior business day and can be booked up to 1 week in advance.

name: Brookings Area Transit Authority (BATA)
operator: Brookings Area Transit Authority (private non-profit, SDDOT Section 5311 subrecipient)
fare: $3.00/trip within Brookings city limits with advance reservation; $9.00/trip same-day within city limits
notes: Door-to-door service the operator describes as 'not limited to who may use it; it is available for everyone' in Brookings County. Typically requires 1-day advance reservation; same-day service available at a higher fare.

name: Brandon Transit
fleet: Two 12-passenger buses, each with 2 wheelchair positions
notes: Curb-to-curb service described by local coverage as 'available to all city residents.' Rides must be scheduled at least 1 day in advance. Owned by the City of Brandon and operated under contract by ROCS (Rural Office of Community Services), a separate multi-county provider also added in this sweep (see ROCS Transit).

name: Community Transit of Watertown/Sisseton
area: 15-county service area in northeast SD centered on Watertown and Sisseton, including Clear Lake and Webster (Brown [excl. City of Aberdeen], Campbell, Clark, Codington, Day, Deuel, Edmunds, Faulk, Grant, Hamlin, parts of Lincoln, Marshall, McPherson, Roberts, and Spink counties)
hours: Watertown office: Mon-Fri 6:00 AM-6:00 PM, Sat 6:00 AM-4:00 PM; Sisseton office: Mon-Fri 7:30 AM-4:00 PM
notes: Nonprofit demand-response dial-a-ride; operator's own site states it serves 'seniors, veterans, students, employees' and general trip purposes with no stated eligibility restriction. Rides must be reserved at least 1 day ahead; fares vary by distance/trip location (amount not published).

name: East Dakota Transit
area: Madison (3-mile radius) and Lake County, SD
fleet: Wheelchair-lift-equipped bus(es); fleet size not specified
notes: Operator states service is open to the public 'regardless of a person's age, handicap, race or sex'; ridership includes general public, school-age, and daycare riders. Rides scheduled by phone one day prior.

name: Palace Transit
notes: Curb-to-curb demand-response service the city's own site describes as open to 'anyone of any age' in Mitchell. Rides must be reserved by 4:00 PM the business day before travel.

name: People's Transit
fare: $3.50 general public; $2.50 seniors 60+ (donation) and youth under 18
notes: Operator states its mission is to serve 'elderly, disabled, and general public.' Rides must be prescheduled; also offers non-emergency medical trips to other eastern SD cities (Sioux Falls, Brookings, Aberdeen, Mitchell, and others).

name: River Cities Public Transit
area: Pierre/Fort Pierre and Hughes, Stanley, Hand, Hyde, Dewey, Ziebach, Haakon, East Pennington, North Jackson, Jones, Lyman, and Minnehaha counties, SD
notes: Nonprofit serving 'individuals with disabilities, the elderly, low income as well as the general public' per operator's site. Offers same-day, on-demand ride requests as well as scheduled-ahead trips (discount for booking by 9pm the prior day). Also operates the Cheyenne River Sioux Tribal Transit contract, added separately in this sweep as Cheyenne River Sioux Transit.

name: ROCS Transit
area: Multi-county south-central/southeastern SD, including Beresford-Alcester, Canton, Charles Mix County, Kingsbury County, Gregory County, Hartford, Miner County, Moody County, Parker, Parkston, Union County, Viborg-Centerville, Wessington Springs, Winner, and Brule-Lyman County
operator: Rural Office of Community Services (ROCS), Inc.
fare: $3 standard contribution in-town for riders 60+; other fares not published
fleet: Wheelchair-accessible vehicles; fleet size not specified
notes: Nonprofit dial-a-ride open to the general public; operator's site describes 'affordable and accessible transportation services' for medical, education, professional, social, shopping and personal needs, free for seniors 60+, Medicaid accepted. Rides scheduled 24 hours ahead. Distinct from Brandon Transit, a separate city-owned system ROCS manages under contract (added separately in this sweep).

name: Southeast Public Transit (Yankton/Vermillion)
area: Yankton and Vermillion, SD (Yankton and Clay counties)
operator: Yankton Transit, Inc., dba Southeast Public Transit
hours: Yankton: Monday-Friday, 5:00 AM-5:00 PM; Vermillion: Monday-Friday, 7:30 AM-5:00 PM
notes: Formed by the merger of the formerly separately-branded Yankton Transit and Vermillion Public Transit systems (both still listed individually as SDDOT Section 5311 rural subrecipients); open to the public with no stated eligibility restriction found. Yankton service requires booking the day before; Vermillion accepts same-day requests 'dependent upon availability' at a higher fare.

name: Prairie Hills Transit
area: Black Hills region: Butte, Custer, Fall River, Lawrence, Meade, Perkins, and part of Pennington counties, SD (16 communities including Belle Fourche, Deadwood, Spearfish, and Sturgis)
operator: West River Transit Authority, Inc., dba Prairie Hills Transit
notes: Grew from a senior-only shuttle (Spearfish Senior Transportation, est. 1989) into a general-public county-wide door-to-door system; site states service is provided to 'students, elderly, individuals with disabilities, and the general public.' One business day's notice required.

name: Cheyenne River Sioux Transit
area: Eagle Butte and surrounding communities, Cheyenne River Reservation, SD
operator: River Cities Public Transit (operates under contract for the Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe)
hours: Monday-Friday, 5:00 AM-6:00 PM; Saturday, 6:00 AM-3:00 PM
notes: Open to the general public with no stated eligibility restriction per operator's site. Discounted fare for booking at least 1 day ahead; same-day service available based on driver availability at a higher rate. 23,481 annual unlinked passenger trips (2024 NTD data).

name: Sisseton Wahpeton Oyate Transit
area: Lake Traverse Reservation, SD (Sisseton and surrounding communities)
operator: Sisseton Wahpeton Oyate Department of Transportation
fare: $3 round-trip (7 mi or less); $5 round-trip (over 7 mi); grocery trips within city limits free via store partnership
hours: Monday-Friday, 6:00 AM-6:00 PM; office 8:00 AM-4:30 PM
notes: Tribal DOT states its mission covers 'our traveling Oyate and General Public,' and is described in secondary sources as the sole source of public transportation on the Lake Traverse Reservation. Booking window (advance vs. same-day) not explicitly confirmed on the operator's own site; Advance is used here as a reasonable inference from phone-dispatch demand-response service consistent with peer SD tribal transit systems -- verify directly before relying on it.

name: Rosebud Sioux Tribe Transit
area: Rosebud Reservation, Todd and Mellette counties, SD
fleet: 14 revenue vehicles, 9 operated in maximum service (2022 NTD data)
notes: NTD reports this as a demand-response public transit agency with 54,019 annual unlinked passenger trips (2022 data), confirming it is an operating public transit system rather than just a roads department. Eligibility ('who can ride') and booking/scheduling window could not be confirmed from the tribe's own site (transportation section not found / page unreachable); inclusion is inferred from NTD mode classification and consistency with peer general-public SD tribal transit systems (Cheyenne River, Sisseton-Wahpeton) rather than direct verification. HIGH PRIORITY: confirm eligibility language directly with the tribe before treating this row as settled in-scope.

name: UTA On Demand
area: South Davis County, Salt Lake City Westside, Southern Salt Lake County, Tooele County, and West Provo/Orem (Wasatch Front); North Utah County zone (Eagle Mountain, Saratoga Springs, Lehi, American Fork, Pleasant Grove, Lindon, Highland, Cedar Hills, Alpine) launching Aug 17, 2026
fare: $2.50 standard / $1.00 reduced fare; includes transfer to bus/TRAX/FrontRunner within 2 hours
hours: Varies by zone; no Sunday service
funding: Local, State (North Utah County zone sponsored by Utah County and UDOT; broader program funded through UTA's operating budget; federal FTA contribution plausible but not itemized on official materials)
fleet: Via-operated vans (WAV); fleet size not specified; Tooele County zone switched to all-electric vehicles per a 2020s UTA announcement
notes: 645,308 boardings in 2025 (13.6% year-over-year growth per UTA's 2025 rider-data report, published Jan 2026); over 2 million total riders since program launch. Originally piloted Nov 2019 in southern Salt Lake County (Bluffdale, Draper, Herriman, Riverton, South Jordan; ~65 sq mi, 7 TRAX/FrontRunner stations); has since expanded to 5 concurrent zones with a 6th (North Utah County) launching Aug 2026. Treated as a single multi-zone system, consistent with how High Valley Transit Micro's multiple microzones are handled in this database.

name: Connect Pool (formerly CVTD POOL)
area: Providence, Millville, River Heights, Cliffside, and portions of Logan, Cache County
operator: Connect Public Transit (Cache Valley Transit District)
vendor: Via (per current official site branding, "Connect On-Demand by Via"); Ecolane was reported as the vendor at the service's 2023 launch — see concerns.csv for this discrepancy
hours: Monday-Friday 6:15 AM-8:45 PM; Saturday 9:45 AM-6:30 PM; no Sunday service
fleet: 2 wheelchair-accessible vans (7-passenger capacity each) with bike racks, at 2023 launch; current fleet size not confirmed
notes: Launched Feb 6, 2023 as "POOL" to cover four bus routes being removed or modified; initial expectation of 50-80 trips/day. Cache Valley Transit District rebranded as "Connect Public Transit" in 2024; the on-demand service continues under "Connect Pool"/"Connect On-Demand" branding with expansion plans noted on the operator's site.

name: Moab Area Transit (MAT)
area: Moab and surrounding service area, Grand County
hours: Peak season (Mar 16-Oct 15): 9 AM-9 PM daily; Off-peak (Oct 16-Mar 15): Monday-Friday 9 AM-5 PM, on-demand only (fixed Main Street route suspended off-peak)
funding: State, Federal, Local ($10 million Utah Hotspot grant administered by UDOT; FTA; City of Moab; Grand County)
notes: Launched March 16, 2023 as Moab's first-ever public transit service; door-to-door on-demand microtransit supplements a fixed Main Street route. Only the on-demand/door-to-door component is in scope for this database; the fixed Main Street route is out of scope as fixed-route service.

name: Fond du Lac Area Shared-Ride Taxi
area: City of Fond du Lac and Village of North Fond du Lac, WI (pickup/dropoff more than 1/4 mile from a fixed bus route)
operator: Private taxi contractor under agreement with Fond du Lac Area Transit (contractor name not disclosed on source page)
window: Advance (phone reservation required by 4:30pm the weekday prior to travel; same-day requests accommodated based on driver availability)
fare: $5.00 (ages 5-64); $4.00 with monthly pass; $3.00 for seniors 65+ with Medicare, individuals with disabilities, and children under 5 with adult
hours: Monday-Friday 6:00am-6:30pm (no weekend service; limited holiday exceptions for Christmas Eve/Day and New Year's Eve/Day)
funding: Not specified (Wisconsin's statewide Wis. Stat. 85.20 shared-ride taxi program is typically funded via WisDOT + FTA Section 5311/5307 + local match, but funding was not itemized on this source page)
notes: Part of Wisconsin's statewide Wis. Stat. 85.20 shared-ride taxi program; supplements Fond du Lac Area Transit's fixed-route bus network by covering pickup/dropoff points more than 1/4 mile from a fixed route. Curb-to-curb, phone-dispatched, open to the general public with no eligibility-certification requirement found.

name: Wisconsin Rapids Shared-Ride Taxi
area: City of Wisconsin Rapids and up to 5 miles outside city limits, WI
operator: Running Inc. (private contractor) under agreement with City of Wisconsin Rapids
vendor: Not specified (Running Inc. operates its own online booking portal at runninginc.net; not a known third-party microtransit software vendor)
window: Advance (reservation required; exact advance-notice window not published on source page)
funding: Local (City of Wisconsin Rapids transportation grant, per source page); state/federal funding plausible under WI's statewide shared-ride taxi program but not itemized on source page
notes: Door-to-door shared-ride service; priority given to in-city passengers over the 5-mile extended zone. Multiple passengers may share a single trip via 'most appropriate route' dispatching; no guaranteed arrival time noted for mid-trip destination changes. General public, no eligibility restriction found on source page.

name: Waupun Shared-Ride Taxi
area: City of Waupun, WI, plus trips outside the service area at a per-mile rate
operator: Brown Cab Service, Inc. (contracted by City of Waupun)
window: Advance (phone reservation required; exact advance-notice window not published — source instructs riders to 'call to verify in advance')
fare: $4.00 regular; $3.00 elderly/disabled/student; $9.75 agency; $2.75 additional passenger to same destination; $10.00 package delivery; $6.00 late night; $2.50/mile outside service area (2024 rates)
hours: Mon-Thu 6am-6pm; Fri 6am-6pm and 9pm-2:30am; Sat 9am-2pm and 9pm-2:30am; closed Sunday (holiday exceptions apply; hours subject to change)
funding: State, Federal (source states only 'state and federal funding'; consistent with the WI Wis. Stat. 85.20 shared-ride taxi program pattern but not itemized)
notes: Source page explicitly states the service operates with 'no discrimination or restriction on trip purpose' — general public. Operated by Brown Cab Service under contract with the City of Waupun, part of the same multi-city Brown Cab shared-ride taxi network that also serves Medford, WI, and reportedly Edgerton, Fort Atkinson, Jefferson, Lake Mills, Monroe, Ripon, Sauk Prairie, and Whitewater, WI (those additional cities were identified via Brown Cab's own service-area list but not individually verified in this pass and are not yet added to the database).

name: Medford Shared-Ride Taxi Service
area: City of Medford and a 5-mile radius, WI
operator: Brown Cab Services, Inc. (contracted by City of Medford)
window: Advance (reservation required; exact advance-notice window not published on source page)
fare: Not specified (source describes 'subsidized fare rides' and directs riders to Brown Cab's website for current rates)
funding: City of Medford General Fund, State of Wisconsin DOT 85.20 Program, FTA Section 5311 Program, and rider fares (all confirmed on source page)
notes: Demand-response service described as serving 'citizens in the community' (general-public framing; no eligibility-certification language found on source page). Operated by Brown Cab Services under contract with the City of Medford, part of the same multi-city Brown Cab shared-ride taxi network that also serves Waupun, WI.

name: Viroqua-Westby Shared-Ride Taxi
area: City of Viroqua and City of Westby, WI
operator: Passenger Transit, Inc. (contracted by City of Viroqua and City of Westby)
window: Advance (reservation required; exact advance-notice window not published)
fare: $3.75 adult, $2.50 senior/disabled, $2.75 student, plus $7.00 Viroqua-Westby inter-city surcharge (current rates per City of Viroqua fare schedule; proposed increase to $4.00/$3.00/$3.00/$4.00 effective Jan 1, 2026)
hours: Not specified (operator describes overall service as 'seven days per week, 365 days per year'; office hours Mon-Fri 8:00am-4:00pm; per-city daily service-hours not published)
fleet: Wheelchair-accessible vehicles available per operator site; fleet size not specified
notes: General-public eligibility confirmed directly on operator Passenger Transit Inc.'s own site (passengertransit.net), which states no restriction to a specific eligible population and offers wheelchair-accessible vehicles. Passenger Transit also operates a third shared-ride taxi city, Watertown, WI, not independently verified or added in this pass.

name: CARTS Dial-A-Ride
area: Central Kenai Peninsula: Soldotna, Kenai, Funny River, Kasilof, Nikiski, Sterling, and surrounding areas (13-zone service area)
operator: Central Area Rural Transit System, Inc. (CARTS)
fare: $25 one-way under 20 miles / $50 one-way 20+ miles; +$25 for an attendant; specific fare schedule per operator's Fares page
hours: Monday-Saturday, 24 hours/day, except observed holidays (reservation office hours Mon-Sat 9am-5pm; rides must be scheduled by close of business the day before travel)
funding: Federal (FTA 5311, FTA 5310), State, Local (Kenai Peninsula Borough)
fleet: Not specified (historically 13-passenger vans plus wheelchair-accessible minivans; current fleet count not published)
notes: Operator states 'CARTS provides public transportation for everyone' (open to general public, not ADA/senior-restricted). Nonprofit incorporated Jan 2000; service began operating later that year. Early operating history (2001) cited ~2,000 rides/month; current ridership not published.

name: KATS Dial-A-Ride
area: City of Kodiak and specified areas outside city limits, Kodiak Island Borough
operator: Senior Citizens of Kodiak, Inc. (program administrator); operated under contract by First Student Inc.
booking: Phone (486-8308); registration required by phone or in person before first ride
fare: $2.00 per one-way ride (pre-purchased e-pass or exact cash)
hours: Monday-Friday 6:30 AM-6:30 PM; Saturday-Sunday 10:00 AM-3:00 PM
notes: Operator states 'Everyone is eligible' to ride (explicitly open to general public, not ADA/senior-restricted). Rides must be scheduled a day or more in advance; cancellations require 2+ hours' notice; children under 10 cannot ride unaccompanied.

name: GIFT On-Demand
operator: City of Idaho Falls (Greater Idaho Falls Transit)
funding: FTA grant ($4.2M) plus Idaho Transportation Department ($327,000); operating as a 2-year pilot
notes: Replaced fixed-route service that ended in 2019. Open to general public with no age/disability eligibility restriction; rides can be booked same-day or up to 2 weeks in advance via the GIFT On-Demand app.

name: VRT On-Demand (Nampa/Caldwell)
area: Nampa, Caldwell, and surrounding Canyon County
fare: $1.50 single ride / $2.50 day pass (standard VRT fare)
notes: General-public on-demand microtransit zone booked via the "VRT Booking" app, rideVRT.org, or phone. Technology vendor inferred as possibly Via from the booking-page URL structure but not independently confirmed; recorded as Not specified per project convention.

name: SPOT Boundary County Demand-Response
area: Boundary County (Bonners Ferry), with Thursday service to Sandpoint/Bonner County
hours: Tue/Wed/Fri 9am-3pm (Boundary County); separate Thursday route to Sandpoint
notes: General-public curb-to-curb demand-response; site instructs riders to call at least a day in advance. Distinct from SPOT's separate fixed routes in Bonner County (Sandpoint/Dover/Ponderay/Kootenai, out of scope as fixed-route) and a separate ADA paratransit program (also out of scope).

name: Pocatello Regional Transit Rural Door-to-Door
area: Bannock, Bear Lake, Bingham, Caribou, Franklin, Oneida, and Power counties (outside the Pocatello/Chubbuck urban area)
fare: $2 one-way (general public); $2 suggested donation for riders 60+; $40/20-ride punch card
notes: Operator's site states rural-area riders are eligible without ADA/age certification ("All residents living beyond Pocatello/Chubbuck but within PRT's service area... are eligible to ride"), distinct from PRT's separate in-town door-to-door service which IS restricted to ADA-certified riders and seniors 60+ (excluded from this database). Exact advance-notice window not confirmed from the source page.

name: Lewiston Transit Dial-A-Ride
notes: Source describes service as "available to the general public, no membership required," with ride priority given first to ADA-qualified riders, then seniors 60+, then general public -- the same priority-order pattern already used to justify including SMART Transit Dial-A-Ride (Twin Falls) in this database. Primary source page (PDF) could not be fully retrieved during this pass; most operational fields unconfirmed.

name: Standing Rock Public Transit
area: Sioux, Morton, and Burleigh counties (ND) and Corson and Walworth counties (SD); serves 9 communities including Fort Yates
notes: Described as "open to all"/general public by a secondary aggregator (Helpline Center) and by partner agency Bis-Man Transit's summary page, neither of which is the tribe's own primary source. The tribe's own program materials (a Sitting Bull College PDF) were image-based and unreadable via automated fetch, and the NTD agency profile page was blocked. Recommend a human verify general-public eligibility directly before treating this as fully confirmed.

name: NW (Northwest) Dakota Public Transit
area: City limits of Williston and Watford City (Williams and McKenzie counties)
operator: Williston Council for the Aging, dba NW Public Transit
fare: $3 (general public); free for seniors and Williams County VA-card veterans
hours: Williston Mon-Fri 6:30am-5:30pm; Watford City Mon-Fri 7:30am-4pm and 5pm-9pm
notes: Operated by a senior-services nonprofit, but the eligibility language describes a general-public $3 fare service with senior/veteran fare waivers as add-ons rather than access gates. Reservations preferred 48+ hours in advance; airport trips require 1 week notice. Operator name ("Council for the Aging") suggests a possible senior focus -- worth a human sanity check against the SMART Transit / Lewiston precedent for priority-vs-restriction language.

name: Wildrose Public Transportation
area: Northwest ND: Wildrose, Alamo, Zahl, Tioga, Ray, McGregor, Epping, Fortuna, Ambrose, Crosby, Noonan, Columbus, Lignite, Flaxton, Bowbells, Kenmare; longer routes to Williston, Minot, and Bismarck
fleet: 3 vehicles: 10-passenger van, 12-passenger bus, and a minivan, all wheelchair lift/ramp equipped
notes: General-public service; seniors in Divide/Williams counties are sponsored via a separate Senior Citizen grant (a subsidy, not an access restriction). Also bills VA/Medicaid as one of several payer types for eligible riders, alongside general fare-paying public.

name: MyBlue On-Demand Microtransit
area: Five zones: Espanola (15-mile radius of transit center), Taos (2-mile radius of Route 340), Pojoaque/Nambe, Edgewood, and La Cienega -- spanning Santa Fe, Rio Arriba, Taos, and Los Alamos counties
fare: $1.00 per trip (most zones); free within the Pojoaque/Nambe zone; free for certified ADA paratransit riders and for military/veterans
hours: Mon-Fri 6am-6pm (most zones); Edgewood 7:30am-5:30pm; La Cienega temporarily reduced to 6-7:30am and 3:30-4:30pm due to a stated staffing shortage as of Dec 2025
fleet: Blue Bus / MyBlue microtransit vans; vehicle count not specified
notes: General-public zone-based on-demand microtransit requested via the "MyBlue North Central RTD" app or phone; no walk-ups permitted. Distinct from NCRTD's separate ADA-only paratransit program, which is excluded from this database as eligibility-restricted.

name: RideKC Micro Transit (Johnson County)
area: Johnson County, KS — approx. 80-square-mile '499 Micro Transit' zone including Downtown Overland Park, Mission Transit Center, and KU Edwards Campus
operator: Johnson County Transit (RideKC / Johnson County Government)

Part of the multi-county RideKC On-Demand family (see also Johnson County and Leavenworth rows).

name: OCCK OnDemand (Salina CityGo)
vendor: Transitioned software providers over time (TransLoc/Transit app integration circa 2022; new OnDemand-specific platform as of Dec. 15, 2025; specific current vendor name not confirmed)

name: Reno County Area Transit (RCAT) Demand Response
area: Hutchinson and South Hutchinson, Reno County, KS

notes: Door-to-door call-in service, distinct from Reno County's fixed-route and ADA paratransit programs; open to general public. Reservations may be made up to 7 days in advance, or next-day/same-day if availability permits; return trips must be scheduled and paid separately.

name: CART (Cooperative Alliance for Regional Transportation)
area: Derry, Hampstead, Londonderry, and Salem, NH (curb-to-curb)
fare: $2.00 per adult trip; $1.00 per child (ages 5–15); under 5 free; exact cash only

notes: Curb-to-curb demand-response service; MTA's own service page states rides must be scheduled at least one business day (up to one week) in advance, with 24-hour cancellation notice required; no eligibility restriction language found — appears open to general public. MTA/CART also runs a separately branded Salem Shopper Shuttle with 3/4-mile route deviation on a fixed schedule (Mon/Wed/Fri) — that service is a fixed-route variant and is excluded per project precedent; only the curb-to-curb CART demand-response service is represented here.

name: SCS Dial-A-Ride (Claremont)
fare: Standard SCS Transportation Program fares apply (not separately itemized for Dial-A-Ride: roughly $1.50 within-town / $2.50 town-to-town / $10 eight-punch pass elsewhere on SCS's fare schedule)

SCS also operates a separate 3/4-mile route-deviation service in Charlestown/Claremont/Newport, which is excluded per project precedent (fixed-route variant); only the Claremont Dial-A-Ride demand-response component is represented here.

name: RTC OnDemand
area: Southwest Las Vegas Valley and West Henderson, Clark County, NV (approx. 32–33 square mile zone, expanded multiple times since launch)
operator: Regional Transportation Commission of Southern Nevada (RTC)
fare: $2.00 per ride for general riders; $3.00 for certified paratransit riders using the same on-demand fleet
funding: CARES Act / American Rescue Plan federal stimulus funds cited at launch (2021); current recurring funding not itemized
fleet: Shared fleet serving both general on-demand and ADA-certified paratransit riders via RideCo's Microtransit Service Integrator; vehicle count not specified
notes: Launched Sunday, August 8, 2021. Genuinely open to the general public (not restricted to paratransit-certified riders) — general riders are dropped at points of interest/transit stops while paratransit-certified riders in the same zone receive door-to-door service; ~50,000 total trips (fixed-route transfers, certified paratransit, and student riders combined) reported since inception as of a Jan. 2023 RTC committee presentation. This is distinct from RTC's separate ADA complementary paratransit program (RTC ACCESS), which remains out of scope for this database. rtcsnv.com blocks automated fetch (403); details sourced from RideCo's own case study/webinar, a public RTC committee PDF (via rtcsnv.civicweb.net), and Nevada Current news coverage.

notes: This is the SAME underlying bi-state Lake Link service already recorded in this database under CA (row 'Lake Link', South Lake Tahoe) — added here as a mirrored NV row per the established bi-state precedent (see 'Access AT' NH/VT) because Lake Link's service area demonstrably includes real Nevada communities (Round Hill, Zephyr Cove, Stateline, Douglas County), not just California. Open to both residents and visitors; children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult; only service animals permitted.

Distinguished by COIC/CET's own materials from Bend Dial-a-Ride and RIDE Assist, which are restricted to qualifying seniors/disabled riders (excluded, out of scope).

Per SETD's own Feb 26, 2026 Board of Commissioners item, the program 'has ended and we are studying data to demonstrate value for future sustainability' (255 total trips, 26 unique riders, ~$52/ride operating cost over the pilot). Language is exploratory about relaunch, not a confirmed permanent shutdown; no evidence of relaunch found as of this research (July 2026).

name: Basin Connect South

name: Basin Connect North
area: Not specified — rural Klamath County north of Klamath Falls; specific towns not published on operator's site
booking: Not specified (likely phone, 541-883-2877, shared dispatch line with Basin Connect South — not independently confirmed)

area: Zones in Dearborn, Troy/Clawson, Pontiac/Auburn Hills, Farmington/Farmington Hills, and the Hall Road corridor (Utica-New Baltimore) — Wayne, Oakland, and Macomb counties

About 80% of riders qualified for reduced fare during the 2020-21 pilot period. Vendor changed from TransLoc to Via at some point post-launch (not independently dated).

name: TheRide FlexRide-East

Sibling service FlexRide-West was discontinued Jan 1, 2026 and replaced by a contracted operator in Pittsfield Township (not in scope, not added).

notes: Launching July 2026 per MTA's own page, with more zones planned; too new for ridership data. Explicitly distinguished on MTA's site from 'Your Ride' (MTA's ADA/senior-restricted paratransit, out of scope) — Genesee Connect eligibility is 'anyone...within one of the zones.'

name: BCGo
operator: Battle Creek Transit (City of Battle Creek) — Calhoun County Coordinated Mobility Pilot

hours: Mon-Fri 5am-7:30pm (current; originally also had Sat 9am-5pm at 2021 launch, which appears to have lapsed)
funding: MDOT grant (Calhoun County Coordinated Mobility Pilot)
notes: Launched March 8, 2021 as a 12-month pilot; has continued operating since. General-public eligibility confirmed (only age-related boarding rules, no eligibility certification). notes: Eligibility directly confirmed on current site: 'all ages without regard to...handicap...or disability' — general public, not certification-gated, despite Medicaid NEMT being one revenue stream. Named 2008 CTAA Rural Community Transportation System of the Year. 2019 directory: 227,868 annual rides (stale figure).

notes: Both programs open to general public residents (Dial-A-Ride: residents of 6 participating municipalities; Flex: all county residents); reduced fare for seniors/veterans/disabled is a discount, not an eligibility gate. Reservations required 3-30 days in advance.

name: Transit Orange Dial-A-Ride Network
area: Nine Orange County municipalities: Goshen, Chester, Highlands, Monroe, Montgomery, Warwick, Wallkill, Newburgh (town), Crawford, Kiryas Joel, and Port Jervis/Deerpark (town-level programs coordinated under the county Transit Orange umbrella)
operator: Orange County Transit / individual town transportation departments (each town operates its own dial-a-ride under the shared Transit Orange umbrella)
fare: Varies by town, $0.50-$6.00 per trip; most areas offer discounted senior/youth fares of $0.50-$1.00
hours: Generally 6:00am-5:00pm weekdays; a few towns (Monroe, Wallkill, Warwick) offer Saturday service
notes: Curb-to-curb, open to the public per the operator's own site; reservations required at least 24 hours in advance (some towns require up to 1 week, e.g. Chester at $4.00 general/$2.00 senior-disabled). name: Move Sullivan
area: Sullivan County (Highland and Delaware runs confirmed; county-wide per operator page)
operator: Sullivan County Division of Community Resources

Operational hours and exact service-area boundary not published on the source page - worth a follow-up call to the department.

name: LANtaFlex
area: Lehigh Valley flex zones: 501 Macungie, 502 Slate Belt, 503 Slatington/Walnutport, 504 Coplay/Egypt Airport, 505 Coopersburg, 506 Bath-Hanoverville-Nazareth, 507 West/South Easton (Lehigh and Northampton counties)

notes: One of PennDOT's 6 statewide microtransit case-study systems (2024 report); operates in defined flex zones (largest over 25 sq mi) with transfer points to fixed LANTA routes, not a route-deviation service; reservations required at least 2 hours ahead, up to 14 days in advance; shares Ecolane software/reporting with LANTA's ADA paratransit and shared-ride service, so some agency-reported data combines microtransit and shared-ride trips.

name: BCTA Connect
area: Beaver County, PA (in-county); out-of-county destination service added Feb 2026

notes: Curb-to-curb on-demand service; app scheduling opened Jan 6 2025; an out-of-county destination expansion went live Feb 2, 2026; a public hearing on further proposed Connect service changes was posted July 22, 2026; local news (not independently accessed) referenced planned expansion of Connect service into Allegheny and Butler counties.

name: Goose Creek Transit
fare: $4.00 general public / $2.50 seniors within Sheridan; $10.00 general public / $7.00 seniors outside city
notes: Dial-a-ride serving downtown Sheridan, Northern Wyoming Community College, Dayton, Ranchester, and Sheridan Memorial Hospital; operated by Sheridan Senior Center but open to all riders — separate general-public and senior fare tiers confirm non-restricted eligibility; reservations must be made a day ahead.

name: Buffalo Area Transit System (BATS)
area: Buffalo & Johnson County, WY; weekly regional trips to Sheridan and Gillette; Kaycee local service
fare: $1.00 local in-town; $2.00 outside town limits; regional (Sheridan/Gillette) fares not specified

fleet: 4 buses (3 serving Buffalo, 1 serving regional routes); wheelchair-accessible vehicles available
notes: Dial-a-ride/on-demand service requiring new rider registration; requests 24-hour advance booking (2-hour minimum if unavoidable); 1-hour cancellation notice required; 3-strikes no-show policy (30-day suspension). New Kaycee local service recently added.

name: STAR Transit Door-to-Door
area: Rock Springs & Green River, Sweetwater County, WY (other county areas with advance notice)
operator: Sweetwater County Transit Authority Resource (STAR Transit)
fare: $2.00 adults/youth over 10; free for seniors 60+; free for up to 2 children under 10 with adult ($1.00 each additional child); $75/month pass
hours: Mon-Fri 7:00am-5:00pm (trips must be scheduled by 5:00pm the day before); closed weekends and holidays
notes: Curb/door pickup and dropoff (riders at apartment/trailer complexes may be asked to board at a designated central point); requires reservations at least 24 hours in advance. STAR also runs a separate fixed 'Stop-to-Stop' route service (Blue/Red Line, Green River Shuttle) not counted as a distinct system here.

name: SafeRide (Laramie)
area: City of Laramie, WY (within city limits)
operator: University of Wyoming Transportation & Parking Services
notes: Curb-to-curb, on-demand; operator's own site states 'SafeRide is open to the public, so anyone can ride!' (children must be accompanied by a parent/guardian); wheelchair accessible with advance notice; distinct from UW's separate fixed-route 'Roundup' bus service.

name: Campbell County Dial-a-Ride
area: Gillette & Campbell County, WY (within city limits and countywide with notice)
fare: Within Gillette: $3.00 (senior/veteran/disabled) or $5.00 (general public) per stop; outside city/within county: $5.00 or $8.00 per stop; punch cards $60 (eligible groups) or $100 (general public) for 20 rides
funding: Federal Transit Administration and State Public Transit programs, administered through WYDOT
notes: Door-to-door service explicitly open to the general public at a higher fare tier alongside a senior/veteran/disabled discount tier; first-time riders must call to register. Distinct from the separate fixed-route Campbell County Public Transportation bus service in Gillette/Wright, not counted here.

name: Cody Senior Center Transportation
area: Cody and up to 10 miles outside city limits, Park County, WY
notes: Operator's own site describes service as available to 'seniors and general public' with a differentiated per-stop fare for each; requires minimum 24-hour advance notice.

name: Gopher
area: Washington County, VT plus three neighboring northern Orange County towns (Barre-Montpelier area)
fare: Tiered: subsidized rides for eligible Vermonters, market-rate taxi-like fares, and contracted corporate/institutional rates; exact dollar amounts not published
notes: Nonprofit 501(c)(3) launched as "Community Rides Vermont," branded Gopher / Gopher-It Rideshare Program. Site states no explicit general-public restriction, and optimal booking window is 2-7 days ahead, but same-day/last-minute requests are explicitly accommodated when possible - recorded as Flexible scheduling window. Also operates as a subcontractor for Medicaid NEMT and Older Adults & People with Disabilities programs; those restricted programs are out of scope, only the general-public rideshare service is represented here.

name: Mountain Town Connector
area: 14 towns in the greater Londonderry/southern Vermont mountain area, incl. Andover, Chester, Chester Depot, Jamaica, Windham, Winhall
funding: Not specified (originated via BDCC Community Facilities Technical Assistance and Training Program on behalf of USDA Rural Development)

Medical-related rides are prioritized but not exclusive. Door-through-door service; drivers may accompany riders into appointments. Single-van fleet limits capacity/scale.

name: MyRide by TVT (Middlebury)
area: Middlebury, VT (Addison County; mapped zone, exact boundary shown only on operator map)
fleet: Vehicles up to 8 passengers, wheelchair-lift accessible, service animals accommodated (shared TVT MyRide fleet spec, per existing Montpelier MyRide row)
notes: Replaced the prior EZ Trip service in Middlebury as of July 15, 2026 (same relaunch date as TVT's Montpelier MyRide zone, already in this CSV as a separate row); bookable 1 hour to 21 days in advance per TVT's own site (differs from Montpelier zone's 15-minute-to-30-day window) with Arrive By/Depart By options. Distinct mapped zone from Montpelier; not a duplicate of the existing MyRide by TVT (Montpelier) row.

name: WinReady

notes: Launched March 25, 2024 as a free, publicly operated point-to-point rideshare service covering the entire City of Winchester; complements the WinTran fixed-route system. Via's ninth tech-enabled transit deployment in Virginia per RideWithVia coverage.

name: MetroFLX
area: Cities of Roanoke and Salem, and Town of Vinton, VA

notes: Launched Jan 22, 2024 to extend service after fixed-route buses stop running and to cover Sunday service; door-to-door within the Roanoke/Salem/Vinton tri-city area. Celebrated 2-year anniversary Jan 2026.

name: GLTC Flex
area: Lynchburg, VA (designated zone incl. Graves Mill Rd, Enterprise Dr, Timberlake Rd, airport area)
fare: Same as standard GLTC bus fare; discounted fares available for eligible riders
notes: Launched Aug 2, 2024 (ribbon-cutting); provides customized point-to-point trips within a designated Lynchburg zone as an alternative to fixed-route buses. Open to the general public.

name: HRT OnDemand
area: Zones in Virginia Beach (~15 sq mi), Newport News (~20 sq mi), Chesapeake (~11.3 sq mi), and Hampton (~5.9 sq mi)
fare: $2/ride; free for qualified paratransit riders and Student Freedom Pass holders; children under 17 free with paying adult
notes: Original Newport News/Virginia Beach pilot ran July 2022-Feb 2023 (26,258 and 13,037 ride requests respectively); relaunched Oct 2024 and expanded to Chesapeake and Hampton Jan 2025. First/last-mile connector to HRT fixed-route bus and light rail. Pilot funding runs through Oct 2026 per one source.

name: LC Transit On Demand
area: Leesburg (~5-6 sq mi zone) and Sterling (~14 sq mi zone), Loudoun County, VA
booking: LC Transit On Demand app, Web (book.lct.rideco.com), Phone (571-258-3464)
hours: Leesburg: Mon-Fri 7am-7pm (weekend service added Jul 5, 2026); Sterling: Mon-Fri 6am-8pm, weekends 8am-10pm

name: Arlington Microtransit (MICRO)
area: Northwest Arlington (two zones: Arlington North and Arlington South), bounded by North Glebe Rd, Langston Blvd, and the county line
fare: $4.50 standard; $2.25 for seniors, persons with disabilities, K-12 students, and Metrorail connections; additional passengers $2.25 each; children under 5 free
notes: Launched Apr 13, 2026 as a stopgap replacing low-ridership fixed-route ART service in northwest Arlington; virtual bus-stop pickup/dropoff model connecting to East Falls Church Metro, Ballston-MU Metro, Virginia Hospital Center, and Madison Community Center. Riders must be 13+ unless with a guardian.

name: Union County On-Demand Micro-Transit Pilot
area: 1.5-mile radius zone centered on Route 28 & South Avenue (County Route 610), Union County, NJ (~35,000 residents)
operator: Union County (River North Transit, LLC / Via)

name: GOTrenton!
area: City of Trenton, NJ and surrounding areas
operator: Isles, Inc. (with NJ Dept. of Environmental Protection support)
funding: State (NJ Dept. of Environmental Protection); Private/Nonprofit (Isles, Inc.)
fleet: Electric shuttles/vans, including Kia Niro EVs
notes: Launched Oct 2023; free/emission-free electric rideshare for the city of Trenton, expanded April 2025; surpassed 100,000 riders per Trenton Journal coverage.

name: ARTS (Aroostook Regional Transportation System)
area: Aroostook County, ME, plus Danforth (Washington County) and Patten (Penobscot County)
fare: Free for low-income residents; other riders pay by check or cash (amount not specified)
hours: Office hours Mon-Fri 6:00am-4:30pm; ride service hours not specified

notes: Door-to-door demand-response service open to the general public (confirmed via multiple sources describing service to "the general public, individuals with disabilities, and the elderly"), not limited to eligibility-certified riders. Requires at least 1 business day advance notice; a few days recommended to guarantee availability.

name: RIDE Hancock
area: Hancock County, IN (Greenfield and surrounding areas; limited out-of-county trips at premium rates)
fare: $4.00 per stop (general public); donation-based for seniors 60+ on essential trips (medical, grocery); $4/stop for seniors on non-essential trips; bulk ride vouchers available
funding: Not specified (FTA Section 5307 pass-through from IndyGo referenced by a secondary source, not confirmed on operator site)
notes: General-public shared-van dial-a-ride operated by the nonprofit Hancock County Senior Services; open to all riders, first-come first-served, call as early as possible to reserve. Limited out-of-county service available at premium rates.

name: Marshall County Rural Transit (MCPT)
area: Marshall County, IN (Plymouth and county-wide); out-of-county trips within a 2-hour radius including South Bend/Mishawaka, Fort Wayne, and Indianapolis
fare: $2.50 per boarding for in-town Plymouth service; out-of-town medical trips for riders 60+ are donation-based (Title III Older Americans Act funding)

funding: United Way of Marshall County, Area 2 Agency on Aging, FTA, INDOT

Also provides separate Medicaid-funded trips for eligible riders.

name: Area 10 Agency on Aging Rural Transit
area: Monroe, Owen, Lawrence, and Putnam counties, IN (plus a deviated fixed-route in Greencastle)
fare: $3.00 one-way / $6.00 round-trip within one county; $6.00 one-way / $12.00 round-trip crossing two counties
hours: Mon-Fri 6:00 AM-6:00 PM (closed holidays); reservation lines Mon-Fri 8:30 AM-4:30 PM
funding: Not specified (federally funded program per operator, exact sources not itemized)
notes: Door-to-door demand-response open to any resident of the four-county service area ('anyone can ride'), though the agency's primary focus is seniors/disabled/caregivers. 3-5 day advance notice required; first-come first-served scheduling. Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult.

name: TRAM (The Ride Around Madison)
area: Rural Madison County, IN (trips must originate or end outside the Anderson urbanized area)
fare: $4.00 per trip (under 60) or $33/month unlimited; $2.50 per trip (60+) or $25/month unlimited
notes: General-public demand-response door-to-door service for rural Madison County residents; distinct from Anderson's in-city CATS fixed routes/paratransit. At least 24 hours advance notice required; payment via voucher purchased from the driver at pickup.

name: Catch-A-Ride (Lifetime Resources)
area: Ripley, Jefferson, Dearborn, Ohio, Switzerland, and Decatur counties, IN (southeast Indiana)
fare: $3.00 base (0-5 miles) plus $0.25/additional mile; reduced $2.00 base fare for seniors 60+, children up to 16, and persons with permanent disabilities; $4.50 base subscription option; group rates available
hours: Mon-Fri 6:00 AM-6:00 PM; call center Mon-Fri 7:00 AM-5:00 PM
funding: Not specified (operates under Title II ADA compliance; also accepts Medicaid/Medicaid Waiver/Medicare/Managed Care as payer sources alongside cash fares)
notes: General-public demand-response covering six southeast Indiana counties; reservations accepted up to 30 days in advance, first-come first-served. Decatur County receives Catch-A-Ride service only (not Lifetime Resources' other programs).

name: MAPS (Metro Area Public Transit System)
area: Joplin, Webb City, Oronogo, Carterville, Duquesne, and Duenweg, MO
fare: $4.00 full fare; $2.00 half fare (seniors 60+, military/veterans, persons with disabilities, Medicare); $2.00 teen fare; $1.00 child (under 12)
notes: Curb-to-curb, prescheduled demand-response covering the greater Joplin metro area, open to the general public; separate paratransit tier serves ADA-eligible riders within 3/4 mile of the fixed bus route. Booking via joplinportal.maps-transit.com or phone.

name: SMTS (Southeast Missouri Transportation Service)
area: 21 counties in Southeast and South Central Missouri (Bollinger, Butler, Carter, Crawford, Dent, Howell, Iron, Madison, New Madrid, Oregon, Pemiscot, Perry, Phelps, Reynolds, Shannon, St. Francois, Ste. Genevieve, Stoddard, Texas, Washington, Wayne)
fare: Not specified (site states fare depends on program eligibility; no flat fare published)
funding: Not specified (nonprofit; approved Medicaid provider; also serves Area Agencies on Aging and other institutional contracts alongside general-public rides)
notes: Door-to-door and some fixed-route service marketed as 'Transportation For Everyone' / 'rural public transportation for everyone' across 21 SE Missouri counties, riders call their local SMTS office to schedule. Also provides Medicaid/NEMT trips as a separate funding stream -- the general-public demand-response tier is the basis for inclusion here.

name: CGCTA Demand Response
fare: Fare varies by trip distance; seniors 60+ ride free within Cape Girardeau County
hours: Mon-Thu 5:00 AM-10:00 PM; Fri-Sat 5:00 AM-12:00 AM; Sun 5:00 AM-2:00 PM
year: Not specified (organization describes itself as having 'over 25 years of service')
notes: Demand-response offered alongside CGCTA's fixed routes; requires 24-hour advance phone reservation. ELIGIBILITY IS AMBIGUOUS across sources: one CGCTA page frames it around 'seniors, individuals with disabilities, and those living in areas with limited fixed-route service,' while the fare structure (a standard fare plus a separate senior-free tier) implies general-public access. Included per the general-public-eligible reading but flagged for human verification -- see concerns.csv.

name: VANLNK
fleet: Smaller vehicles than standard StarTran buses; wheelchair-accessible
notes: Launched April 20, 2020 as a pilot originally designed for disabled/senior riders; broadened to all residents citywide. Door-to-door, app-based on-demand booking anywhere within Lincoln city limits. A separate paratransit-eligible tier can now book up to 7 days in advance through the same app (2025 update) -- that advance option is for ADA-certified riders specifically; the general-public service remains same-day/on-demand.

name: CRANE Public Transit
area: Grand Island Urbanized Area, NE, plus Alda, Wood River, Cairo, and Doniphan
operator: Brown Transit, Inc. (contracted by the City of Grand Island)
fare: $2.00 per one-way trip (CRANE Trip Card scanned on boarding)
notes: Portal-to-portal demand-response open to the general public, 'no membership required'; minimum 24-hour advance reservation, same-day rides only if capacity permits. Approximately 38,000-42,000 trips/year.

name: TeleLift (North Fork Area Transit)
area: Norfolk, Madison, Meadow Grove, Newman Grove, and Battle Creek, NE (Madison County); service reduced to Norfolk city limits as of July 2025 per a 30% state-funding cut
fare: In-town fares start at $2.00 with 24-hour advance reservation; higher fares for county trips and same-day requests
hours: Mon-Fri 7:00 AM-5:00 PM (hours effective July 1, 2025; reservation line Mon-Fri 8:00 AM-4:00 PM)
funding: City of Norfolk, Norfolk United Way, Northeast Community College, local business sponsors, and Nebraska state funding (reduced ~30% per a 2025 service-hours notice)
notes: General-public dial-a-ride operating 3 routes/74 stops within a 30-mile radius of Norfolk; no senior/disability eligibility restriction found. Also operates a separate Regional Flex Route 6 (Norfolk-Wayne) which is a fixed-route-with-deviation service and is NOT included here as it fits this project's route-deviation exclusion.

name: North Platte Public Transit
area: City of North Platte, NE and a 20-mile radius (incl. Lake Maloney, Indian Hills, Sutherland, Hershey, Maxwell)
fare: $1.50-$2.00 one-way in-city with advance reservation; $4.00 for same-day reservation; $5.00-$10.00 per direction for extended/outside-city-limits trips (Sutherland, Hershey, Maxwell up to $10)
hours: Mon-Sat (phone lines close 1 hour before end of service)
funding: Not specified (City of North Platte sponsored)
notes: General-public dial-a-ride ('available to everyone in North Platte and now anyone within a 20 mile radius'); offers both advance-reserved and same-day (higher-fare) trips, hence classified Scheduling Window = Flexible.

name: Columbus Area Transit (CAT)
fare: Punch cards: 5 rides/$10 or 10 rides/$20 (~$2/ride); discounted cards available for eligible riders
funding: Nebraska Department of Transportation (Roads), United Way, City of Columbus budget
notes: Curb-to-curb demand-response 'available to the general public regardless of race, ethnicity, age, sex, or disability' within Columbus city limits; riders must register and schedule at least one day in advance.

name: Fremont Transit Program

fare: $2.00 one-way when reserved 48+ hours in advance; $5.00 for same-day or under-48-hour reservations
year: Not specified (program described as launched 'September 7', year not confirmed)
funding: FTA Section 5311 Rural Public Transportation grant
notes: Door-to-door demand-response explicitly described as available to 'the general public, older adults and persons with disabilities.' One secondary source's framing ('for people whose disabilities prevent them from using fixed-route bus') conflicts with the general-public framing found elsewhere on the same city site; the general-public eligibility language is treated as controlling here per project convention, but flagged for verification.

name: Blue Rivers Public Transportation
area: Gage, Jefferson, Nemaha, Otoe, and Thayer counties, NE (61 communities); plus 2 inter-city routes to Lincoln and Omaha
operator: Blue Rivers Area Agency on Aging
hours: Varies by office (e.g. Beatrice Mon-Fri 8:00 AM-12:00 PM, 12:30-4:30 PM; Auburn, Nebraska City, Fairbury, Hebron, Syracuse each with distinct local hours)

Also operates regular routed service connecting 61 communities plus 2 fixed inter-city routes (Lincoln, Omaha) -- those fixed-route pieces are not the basis for inclusion here, only the demand-response tier.

name: SpartaGo
area: Spartanburg northside and southside neighborhoods, City of Spartanburg
operator: City of Spartanburg / Spartanburg Area Regional Transit Agency (SPARTA)
fare: $2.00 per rider (credit or debit card only)
hours: 6:00 AM-6:00 PM, seven days a week
funding: State (mass transit funds, vehicle purchase); Federal (COVID-era federal transit funds, pilot operations)
fleet: 3 ADA-compliant Ford Transit chassis Mobilitytrans conversion vans
notes: App-based direct pickup/dropoff similar to Uber/Lyft, serving Spartanburg's northside and southside neighborhoods only (not citywide). One-year pilot with a six-month evaluation checkpoint. Vehicle purchase cost ~$344,803; estimated pilot program cost ~$334,442.

name: PDRTA Demand Response
area: Chesterfield, Darlington, Dillon, Florence, Marion, and Marlboro counties (Pee Dee region), SC — named zones include MARTi (Marlboro Co.), DCAT (Dillon Co.), Marion County, Chesterfield East, and Lower Florence
fare: Fare-free (per PDRTA's 2026 service-change notices for converted routes)
hours: Weekdays (varies by zone), approx. 8:00 AM-5:00 PM
notes: Call-ahead (24-hour advance), door-to-door demand response distinct from PDRTA's ADA complementary paratransit. PDRTA's news page shows an active pattern of converting former fixed/commuter routes to this call-ahead model (Chesterfield East 5/1/26; Pamplico-Florence Commuter and MUSC Black River for Lower Florence 4/28/26). A 2024 press release with The Routing Company (Pingo platform) described a planned 'commingled paratransit and on-demand' + workforce-transit deployment, but no live app-based branding was found in PDRTA's own 2026 news archive, so Technology Vendor is left Not specified rather than naming Pingo/TRC.

name: Santee Wateree RTA On-Demand (Sumter)
area: City of Sumter, SC (former Routes 50, 60, 100 corridors: West Liberty St., South Main St., East Liberty St.)
hours: Monday-Friday 6:00 AM-6:00 PM (same-day reservation cutoff 4:00 PM)
notes: Replaced three former fixed routes with a call-ahead, designated-stop on-demand zone service in Sumter (confirmed via SWRTA's own Facebook post; no eligibility restriction stated). SWRTA's separate services page describes a broader 'demand response' offering in Kershaw/Lee/Sumter counties in vaguer terms ('county residents...on a space available basis as a cash passenger') without confirming booking method or fare — this row covers only the confirmed Sumter on-demand zone service; the broader county-wide program may warrant separate follow-up.

name: Aiken County 5311 Rural Transportation
area: Aiken County, SC (outside the urbanized area)
notes: Distinct from Aiken Senior Life Services' other eligibility-restricted offerings (Dial-A-Ride for disabled riders; Title XIX/Medicaid transport) — this program is open to any resident living outside Aiken County's urbanized area, not senior/disability-gated. Trips must be scheduled at least 5 business days in advance; service area is 'anywhere within Aiken County.'

name: Peach Blossom Express
notes: Operator describes the service as meeting 'the transportation needs of all Edgefield County residents' — general public, not senior/disability-restricted despite the operator being the county Senior Citizens Council (same inclusion logic as Bamberg County's Handy Ride, already in this database). Listed on SCDOT's statewide transit-provider directory.

name: Chester Connector (ChescoConnect)
area: Chester County, SC, with expanded coverage into Union County
operator: The Connector (Senior Services, Inc. of Chester County), 501(c)(3) nonprofit
fare: Not specified (described as 'low-cost'; discounted rates for seniors 65+, ADA-eligible riders 18-64, and Medicaid recipients; general-public riders pay full fare)
hours: Monday-Friday, plus Saturday within Chester County; office hours Mon-Fri 8:00 AM-4:30 PM
year: 1973 (organization founded; demand-response service start date not separately confirmed)

notes: Curb-to-curb demand response confirmed open to anyone age 12+ via the operator's own 'Who Can Ride' page (chesco.org/5326/Who-Can-Ride): general-public riders pay full fare while seniors/ADA-eligible/Medicaid riders receive reduced or program-funded rates. Not restricted to a certified eligibility class.

name: York County Access
area: York County and City of Rock Hill, SC (Ride-to-Work limited to Rock Hill city limits)
operator: York County Council on Aging (in cooperation with York County and City of Rock Hill)
hours: Essential Service Mon-Fri 6:00 AM-6:00 PM; Ride-to-Work Mon-Fri 5:30-9:00 AM and 3:30-6:00 PM
notes: Confirmed general public eligibility (residents of York County/Rock Hill) via operator's own county government page. 'Essential Service' (48-hr advance) covers medical-related trips countywide; 'Ride-to-Work' (24-hr advance) covers employment trips within Rock Hill. Its role is expanding following Rock Hill's May 2026 shutdown of its fixed-route MyRide bus system, per WBTV coverage.

name: RPT GO
area: South Rochester, MN microtransit zone (bounded south of 12th St SE, west of 50th Ave SE, east of Badger Run Creek; hubs at Cub Foods SE, RCTC, Mayo High School, Quarry Hill Park, Fairgrounds Park & Ride; expanded 2026 to include Central Park)
vendor: Spare (Spare Labs) -- inferred from Google Play package name com.sparelabs.platform.rider.rptgo, not independently confirmed on the city's own site
fare: $3.00 per ride; free for children under 5
fleet: Electric mid-size SUVs and hybrid-fuel vans, wheelchair accessible
notes: Launched October 2024 as a one-year pilot (through September 2025); pilot concluded on schedule and the city expanded the zone afterward rather than ending it, per a March 2026 service update. Distinct from Rochester's ZIPS Paratransit, which is eligibility-restricted to riders with disabilities and out of scope.

name: goMARTI
area: 20-square-mile Grand Rapids, MN service area with ~70 pickup/dropoff points; by 2025 expanded to connect Grand Rapids with rural and tribal communities along Highway 2
operator: City of Grand Rapids / Minnesota Department of Transportation (MnDOT), public-private partnership
vendor: Via (goMARTI 2.0 platform); originally launched on May Mobility's autonomous-vehicle platform
hours: Monday-Saturday 10:00am-9:00pm, Sunday 8:00am-3:00pm (subject to change for weather/maintenance)
funding: State (MnDOT), Local (City of Grand Rapids), Private (May Mobility, The PLUM Catalyst partnership)
